description: Run a script on Amazon Linux 2023 instances to create symbol details for volatility 3

AccessKeyId.description: (Required) AccesskeyID to store evidence details in S3.

SecretAccessKey.description: (Required) SecretAccessKey to store evidence details in S3

SessionToken.description: (Required) SessionToken to store evidence details in S3.

runCommand: #!/bin/bash
# Amazon Linux 2023 kernel symbol table builder for Volatility 3.
# Unlike the Amazon Linux 2 document this fails loudly: a silently missing
# symbol table makes every later memory investigation return zero rows.
# Upstream versions, pinned. An unpinned clone builds whatever is at the tip of
# the default branch on the day of the incident - into the tooling that produces
# and reads forensic evidence. These match the pins already used by the
# acquisition and investigation documents so that one release means one set of
# tool versions. Note 504ensicsLabs/LiME redirects to jtsylve/LiME, its original
# author; cloning the old path works only while GitHub honours that redirect.
DWARF2JSON_REF=v0.9.0
set -o pipefail
fail() { echo "SYMBOL_BUILD_FAILED: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
kernel_name=$(uname -s)
kernel_release=$(uname -r)
# AL2023 names kernel sub-packages per kernel line (kernel6.18-devel) from 6.12
# onwards, but keeps the unversioned name (kernel-devel) on the 6.1 line.
kernel_line=$(uname -r | cut -d. -f1,2)
echo "building volatility3 symbols for ${kernel_name}-${kernel_release} (line ${kernel_line})"
grep -q 'platform:al2023' /etc/os-release || fail "not an Amazon Linux 2023 instance: $(. /etc/os-release; echo $PRETTY_NAME)"
# /tmp is a RAM-backed tmpfs on AL2023 capped at ~50% of memory; the debuginfo
# package and the generated ISF JSON do not reliably fit there.
workdir=/var/tmp/forensic-symbol-builder
sudo rm -rf $workdir && mkdir -p $workdir && cd $workdir || fail 'cannot create work directory'
sudo dnf install -y -q git golang || fail 'unable to install git/golang'
sudo dnf groupinstall -y -q 'Development Tools' || sudo dnf install -y -q gcc make || fail 'unable to install build tools'
install_kernel_pkg() {
# $1 = suffix (devel|debuginfo); try the versioned name then the legacy name
sudo dnf --enablerepo='*debuginfo' install -y -q "kernel${kernel_line}-$1-${kernel_release}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "installed kernel${kernel_line}-$1-${kernel_release}"; return 0; }
sudo dnf --enablerepo='*debuginfo' install -y -q "kernel-$1-${kernel_release}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "installed kernel-$1-${kernel_release}"; return 0; }
return 1
install_kernel_pkg devel || fail "no kernel-devel package for ${kernel_release}"
install_kernel_pkg debuginfo || fail "no kernel-debuginfo package for ${kernel_release}; the amazonlinux-debuginfo repo may not yet carry this kernel build"
vmlinux=/usr/lib/debug/lib/modules/${kernel_release}/vmlinux
test -f $vmlinux || vmlinux=/usr/lib/debug/usr/lib/modules/${kernel_release}/vmlinux
test -f $vmlinux || fail "debug vmlinux not found for ${kernel_release}"
systemmap=/boot/System.map-${kernel_release}
test -f $systemmap || fail "System.map not found for ${kernel_release}"
cd $workdir
git clone --depth 1 --branch "$DWARF2JSON_REF" https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/dwarf2json.git || fail "dwarf2json clone of $DWARF2JSON_REF failed"
cd dwarf2json
sudo env PATH=$PATH HOME=/root go build || fail 'dwarf2json build failed'
echo 'dwarf2json build done'
# Name the ISF file <uname -s>-<uname -r>.json so that the memory load
# investigation document finds it from the capture's S3 object metadata.
symbol_file=${kernel_name}-${kernel_release}.json
./dwarf2json linux --system-map $systemmap --elf $vmlinux > $workdir/$symbol_file || fail 'dwarf2json symbol generation failed'
# Shape is not content: a dwarf2json run that was killed part way through
# leaves a file of about 134 bytes whose maps are all empty, and that passes an
# 'is the key present' test while making every later plugin return zero rows.
# Require populated maps plus what volatility3 actually reads:
# symbols.linux_banner.constant_data, which is the only thing automagic can
# match an ISF to a capture with (see framework/automagic/symbol_cache.py),
# init_task to walk processes, and the task_struct definition. The path goes in
# through argv rather than through the program text.

python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); s=d.get("symbols") or {}; b=d.get("base_types") or {}; u=d.get("user_types") or {}; banner=(s.get("linux_banner") or {}).get("constant_data"); sys.exit(0 if (s and b and u and banner and "init_task" in s and "task_struct" in u) else 1)' "$workdir/$symbol_file" || fail 'the generated symbol table is not a usable volatility3 ISF file'
echo "symbol build done: $(ls -lh $workdir/$symbol_file | awk '{print $5}')"
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID={{AccessKeyId}}
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY={{SecretAccessKey}}
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN={{SessionToken}}
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION={{Region}}
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 20
aws s3 cp $workdir/$symbol_file s3://{{s3bucket}}/volatility3/symbols/$symbol_file --acl bucket-owner-full-control || fail 's3 upload of symbol table failed'
echo "s3 copy complete: s3://{{s3bucket}}/volatility3/symbols/$symbol_file"
sudo rm -rf $workdir
exit 0;
